questions.question: How many elements are listed in the modern periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**118 elements**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **118 elements** are currently listed in the modern periodic table.
 
• The modern periodic table is organized based on the **atomic number** of elements, which is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• Elements are arranged in rows called **periods** and columns called **groups** or families, where elements in the same group have similar chemical properties.
 
• The periodic table helps in understanding the **properties, behaviors, and trends** of elements, such as electronegativity, ionization energy, and atomic radius.
 
• It was developed based on the work of several scientists, most notably **Dmitri Mendeleev**, who is credited with creating the first widely recognized periodic table.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **modern periodic table** is a tabular arrangement of chemical elements, ordered by their **atomic number, electron configuration, and recurring chemical properties**.
 
• The rows of the table are called **periods**, and the columns are called **groups**.
 
• Elements are presented in order of increasing atomic number, which is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The periodic table is a fundamental tool in the field of **chemistry** and is used extensively by chemists to predict the properties of elements and their compounds.
 
• The table has been expanded and refined over time as new elements have been discovered and new theoretical insights have been developed.

questions.question: In which state of India is shifting cultivation known as Bringa?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the state of **Odisha**, **shifting cultivation** is referred to as **Bringa**.
 
• This form of agriculture involves **clearing a piece of land by cutting down and burning the vegetation**, then using the cleared land for cultivation.
 
• Shifting cultivation is a traditional practice among various indigenous communities in Odisha.
 
• It is primarily practiced in the hilly and forested regions of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting cultivation**, also known as** slash-and-burn agriculture**, is a method where farmers rotate the fields they cultivate rather than farming the same land continuously.
 
• This practice helps in maintaining soil fertility and controlling pests and weeds naturally.
 
• However, it can **lead to deforestation and soil erosion** if not managed sustainably.
 
• Efforts are being made to introduce more sustainable agricultural practices among the communities practicing shifting cultivation.

questions.question: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**cytokinesis**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cytokinesis** is the process during cell division where the **cytoplasm of a parental cell is divided between two daughter cells**.
 
• The formation of the **phragmoplast** occurs during cytokinesis in plant cells.
 
• The phragmoplast is a structure that serves as a **scaffold for cell plate assembly** and subsequent formation of a new cell wall separating the two daughter cells.
 
• It is essential for the successful completion of cell division in plants, ensuring that each daughter cell receives the necessary cellular components.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell division** consists of two main processes: mitosis (karyokinesis) and cytokinesis.
 
• **Mitosis** is the division of the nucleus, whereas **cytokinesis** is the division of the cytoplasm.
 
• In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs through the formation of a cleavage furrow that pinches the cell into two.
 
• In plant cells, the **phragmoplast** guides the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a separating cell wall.
 
• The **G0 phase** is a resting phase where the cell is not actively preparing to divide.
 
• The **S phase** is the part of the cell cycle where DNA replication occurs.

questions.question: In which type of forests are Mahogany, Rosewood and Cinchona trees found in India?

__
 
• **Mahogany, Rosewood, and Cinchona trees** are typically found in **Tropical Evergreen forests** in India.
 
• Tropical Evergreen forests are characterized by **high rainfall, usually above 200 cm annually, and a warm climate.**
 
• These forests are dense, multi-layered, and host a diverse range of flora and fauna.
 
• They are primarily found in regions such as the **Western Ghats, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and parts of northeastern India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tropical Evergreen forests are also known as **rainforests** due to their lush, green appearance throughout the year.
 
• The continuous canopy in these forests allows little sunlight to reach the ground, resulting in a sparse undergrowth.
 
• These forests play a crucial role in maintaining ecological balance and are vital for biodiversity conservation.
 
• Other notable trees found in **Tropical Evergreen forests include ebony, rubber, and bamboo**.

questions.question: Why is it important to distinguish between final and intermediate goods/services in national income accounting?

options.text: It helps track changes in consumer preferences and market demand.
This helps in more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.
Provides insight into the distribution of income among different sectors.
It helps to determine the overall quality of goods and services produced.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**This helps in more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **This helps in more accurate measurement of economic growth and productivity.** Accurate national income accounting requires distinguishing between final and intermediate goods/services to avoid double counting.
 
• **Final goods are those that are purchased for consumption, investment, government spending, or export**, and are not used as inputs in the production of other goods.
 
• **Intermediate goods are used as inputs in the production of final goods**. Including these in national income would result in overestimation of the economic activity.
 
• By only including final goods and services, national income accounting provides a clearer picture of the actual economic output and productivity of a country.
 
• This distinction helps in assessing the true economic growth and development of a nation, guiding policymakers in their decisions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National income accounting** is a system used by governments to measure the economic activity of a country.
 
• It includes the calculation of metrics such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross National Product (GNP), and Net National Income (NNI).
 
• Accurate national income accounting is essential for economic planning and policy formulation.
 
• The distinction between final and intermediate goods is a fundamental principle in the System of National Accounts (SNA), which is the international standard for national income accounting.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a directive principle of state policy?

options.text: Separation of the judiciary from executive
Reside in any part of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reside in any part of India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reside in any part of India** is a fundamental right under **Article 19** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government. They are **not enforceable by any court** but aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• The Directive Principles are listed in **Part IV** of the Constitution, from **Article 36 to 51**.
 
• Examples of Directive Principles include the separation of the judiciary from the executive, the promotion of a uniform civil code, and the protection of monuments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights** are basic human rights guaranteed by the Constitution of India that are enforceable by the courts, subject to certain restrictions.
 
• The **Fundamental Rights **are included in **Part III **of the Constitution, from **Article 12 to 35**.
 
• They ensure civil liberties so that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India.
 
• The Constitution aims to provide a balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles to achieve the goal of a welfare state.

questions.question: In which state is the Sanchi Stupa situated?

• Sanchi is a UNESCO World Heritage site and is famous for its Great Stupa, which is **one of the oldest stone structures in India**.
 
• The Stupa was originally commissioned by the emperor **Ashoka the Great** in the **3rd century BCE**.
 
• The site is a significant Buddhist pilgrimage destination and is renowned for its intricate carvings and historical significance.
 
• The Sanchi Stupa is located near the town of **Raisen** in Madhya Pradesh and is approximately 46 kilometers from the state capital, Bhopal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Sanchi Stupa is a major tourist attraction and draws visitors from all over the world.
 
• The site includes several other stupas, temples, monasteries, and pillars, which were added over the centuries by various patrons.
 
• The gateways and railings of the Stupa are adorned with detailed carvings depicting scenes from the life of the Buddha and various Jataka tales.
 
• Sanchi provides insights into the early development of Buddhist art and architecture in India.
 
• The site is maintained by the** Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**, which has undertaken extensive restoration work to preserve its heritage.

questions.question: Who is the nominal executive authority of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **President** of India is the nominal executive authority of the country.
 
• The President is considered the **ceremonial head of state**, functioning as the symbol of the **unity, integrity, and solidarity of the nation**.
 
• Although the President of India is vested with considerable powers, these are **exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers**.
 
• The President's role is largely ceremonial with real executive power being vested in the Prime Minister and their council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The office of the President of India was established when the country became a republic on **26th January 1950**.
 
• **Article 52** of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a President of India.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, as well as the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The President holds office for a term of** five years** from the date on which they enter upon their office.
 
• In the case of a **vacancy due to death, resignation, or removal**, the **Vice President discharges the duties of the President until a new President is elected**.

• The South China Sea is also known for its biodiversity, hosting a variety of marine species and ecosystems.

• **Manipuri** dance is known for its graceful and fluid movements and is deeply connected with the rituals and traditional festivals of Manipur.
 
• **Chhau** is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial, tribal, and folk origins, often performed during regional festivals.
